name: Park Hyatt Kyoto
positioning: Hillside luxury guesthouse in Kyoto's Higashiyama district, on historic temple grounds beside Ninenzaka with views of Yasaka Pagoda
best_for: Travelers who want to stay among Higashiyama's temples and traditional streets
Guests interested in Kyoto culture, from a historic ryotei to temple tours
Design-minded travelers drawn to tamo wood interiors and local art

facts.text: Park Hyatt Kyoto sits along the cobblestones of Ninenzaka in Higashiyama.
The hotel is located within Kyoto's largest preserved traditional building district.
The hotel is stacked on a hill with a maze of hallways, corridors and garden paths.
The rooms feature interiors crafted from fragrant tamo wood and contemporary art by local artists.
Guest rooms offer a working area and a day bed.
Kyoyamato is a ryotei with a history dating back to 1877.
Yasaka is the hotel's signature teppanyaki restaurant, combining Japanese tradition with French techniques.
Kohaku bar creations highlight Japanese whiskey, sake and gin with seasonal ingredients.
The Living Room offers a five-course afternoon tea by day and becomes a wine and sake bar by night.
In-room dining includes a Japanese breakfast prepared by Sanso Kyoyamato.
World of Hyatt Globalist members and suite guests can enjoy champagne at The Living Room daily.
The Spa and Fitness is available exclusively to hotel guests.

highlights.text: The hotel was built as a partnership of the Pritzker, Takenaka and Kyoyamato families, with Tony Chi as interior designer.
Kyoyamato is set within a group of heritage buildings designated as cultural assets by Kyoto City.
The hotel is set on historic temple grounds with views of Yasaka Pagoda and the machiya townscape.
Guests can take an exclusive tour of Kiyomizu-dera Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Some rooms have a tsuboniwa, a private Japanese garden.

considerations.text: Children under 10 are asked not to attend dinner service at Yasaka.
Access to Kohaku bar is restricted to guests aged 20 and above.
Kyoyamato operates independently and is not eligible for World of Hyatt points.
